name: Teaching models to reason step by step
gist: These papers train models to think through problems more carefully by making them work through intermediate steps before answering, using techniques like reinforcement learning and feedback to improve their reasoning.
explain: When you ask a model a hard math problem or a riddle, the model's default behavior is to rush to an answer immediately. But humans solve hard problems by working through them—writing down intermediate steps, checking if each step makes sense, backtracking when stuck. Papers in this area teach models to do the same thing. Instead of training a model to jump straight from question to answer, researchers set up training so the model learns to generate its own intermediate reasoning first, because working through the steps helps catch mistakes. The model writes out its thinking, then uses that thinking to arrive at the final answer, so each step builds on the previous one. This turns a problem that feels impossible into one the model can actually solve.

The challenge is that simply adding reasoning steps does not automatically work—the model has to learn what kinds of steps are actually helpful, and it has to receive feedback on whether its reasoning was correct. This is why papers in this area lean on reinforcement learning, where the model gets rewarded for reaching the right answer and learns which paths of reasoning lead there. Some papers also use feedback from human annotations or from checking answers against known correct solutions. The insight is that the path matters: two models with the same raw ability might behave very differently if one of them has learned to stop and think while the other just guesses.

The practical result is that models trained this way solve hard problems more often than models that race to answers. Because this works so well, it has become a core technique in modern systems—some of the most capable reasoning models today use reasoning steps as a basic building block. The tricky part is that longer reasoning takes more computation, so researchers also study how to make reasoning efficient and how to know when to use it versus when a direct answer is fast enough.

papers.title: The Pensieve Paradigm: Stateful Language Models with Learned Memory Management

papers.title: ThetaEvolve: Test-time Learning on Open Problems

papers.title: Think Deep, Not Just Long: Measuring LLM Reasoning Effort via Deep-Thinking Tokens

papers.title: Think in Parallel, Answer as One: Logit Averaging for Open-Ended Reasoning

papers.title: Think-While-Generating: On-the-Fly Reasoning for Personalized Long-Form Generation

papers.title: Think-at-Hard: Selective Latent Iterations to Improve Reasoning Language Models

papers.title: Thinking in Flow: A Dissipative Stabilization Operator for Robust Autoregressive Reasoning

papers.title: ThoughtFold: Folding Reasoning Chains via Introspective Preference Learning
papers.contribution: ThoughtFold reduces token usage of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B by approximately 56% while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy.

papers.title: Thoughtbubbles: an Unsupervised Method for Parallel Thinking in Latent Space

papers.title: ThreadWeaver: Adaptive Threading for Efficient Parallel Reasoning in Language Models

papers.title: TikZilla: Scaling Text-to-TikZ with High-Quality Data and Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Prior research has proposed a variety of datasets and modeling approaches for this task.

papers.title: TokUR: Token-Level Uncertainty Estimation for Large Language Model Reasoning

papers.title: Token-Efficient Long-Term Interest Sketching and Internalized Reasoning for LLM-based Recommendation

papers.title: ToolACE-MT: Non-Autoregressive Generation for Agentic Multi-Turn Interaction

papers.title: ToolOrchestra: Elevating Intelligence via Efficient Model and Tool Orchestration

papers.title: Toward Cybersecurity-Expert Small Language Models

papers.title: Towards Execution-Grounded Automated AI Research

papers.title: Towards Strategic Persuasion with Language Models

papers.title: Towards True Speech-to-Speech Models Without Text Guidance

papers.title: Train Once, Answer All: Many Pretraining Experiments for the Cost of One

papers.title: Trust Region Masking for Long-Horizon LLM Reinforcement Learning

papers.title: Unlocking the Power of Multi-Agent LLM for Reasoning: From Lazy Agents to Deliberation

papers.title: Unveiling the Potential of Diffusion Large Language Model in Controllable Generation
